strings.xml.tos_warning: Read this carefully. Whospair works differently from the messaging apps you know, and some of those differences cannot be undone.
strings.xml.tos_s1_body: Whospair has no server. Messages and calls travel directly between devices. Nobody — including us — sits in the middle, stores your data, or can hand it over.
strings.xml.tos_s2_body: No operator stands behind this app. What you send, to whom, and what you do with what you receive is entirely your responsibility. Whospair is a tool: its authors cannot be held liable for how you use it or its consequences.
strings.xml.tos_s3_body: No authority reviews, filters, or removes content. There is no report button that reaches anyone, because there is no one to reach.
strings.xml.tos_s4_body: Messages are end-to-end encrypted (X25519 and AES-256-GCM) and signed. Calls go over Tor, encrypted with a key that changes about every ten seconds.
strings.xml.tos_s5_body: Your identity, contacts, and messages exist only on this device. Uninstalling the app erases them.
strings.xml.tos_s6_body: Your identity is a cryptographic key, not an account. If you lose it, it is gone. There is no password reset, no support line, no backup we can restore.
strings.xml.tos_s7_body: Privacy tools protect legitimate conversations. Using Whospair to break the law remains breaking the law.
strings.xml.tos_s8_body: This software is provided as is, without guarantee of availability, correctness, or fitness for any particular purpose.
strings.xml.tos_s9_body: Encryption protects data in transit. It cannot protect a device that is already compromised by malware, a rootkit, or someone holding it.
strings.xml.tos_s10_body: Continuing means you understand the above, and specifically that a lost identity cannot be recovered.
strings.xml.tos_checkbox: I have read and accept these terms
strings.xml.tos_decline_dialog_body: Whospair cannot run without accepting them. The app will close.
strings.xml.tutorial_p1_body: Messaging and calls that leave no trace on any server, because there is no server.
strings.xml.tutorial_p2_body: There are no usernames or phone numbers. You exchange keys directly.
strings.xml.tutorial_p2_s2: Scan their code, or let them scan yours
strings.xml.tutorial_p2_note: A new identity means a new code. Sharing it again is the only way back.
strings.xml.tutorial_p3_body: Every message carries an expiry from the moment you send it.
strings.xml.tutorial_p3_s2: Type, then pick how long it should live
strings.xml.tutorial_p4_body: Pick the lifetime that fits what you are saying. When it runs out, the message is deleted on both devices.
strings.xml.tutorial_p4_note: Shorter is safer. Anything still on screen is still on disk.
strings.xml.tutorial_p5_body: A few things worth knowing before you begin.
strings.xml.tutorial_p5_f2: Delete a whole conversation at once
strings.xml.tutorial_p5_f3: Lock the app with a PIN
strings.xml.identity_creating_body: Generating a key pair on this device. This takes a moment.
strings.xml.identity_ready_body: Your keys are ready. Now choose your PIN: it seals them. Your QR code will be waiting in Add.
strings.xml.identity_warning: Your private key stays on this device and is never shown. If you lose this device, this identity is gone for good.
strings.xml.discover_subtitle: Show your code to the person, or scan theirs. Face to face, you know who you are talking to.
strings.xml.discover_scan_body: Point the camera at their QR code
strings.xml.discover_manual_title: Or paste a link you received

strings.xml.add_blocked: %1$s is in your contacts but blocked.
strings.xml.add_self: That is your own key. You cannot add yourself.
strings.xml.add_malformed: That key is not valid. A public key is 64 hexadecimal characters.
strings.xml.add_not_whisper: This code is not a Whospair key.
strings.xml.scan_instruction: Point at the QR code you want to add
strings.xml.scan_permission_body: Scanning a code requires the camera. Nothing is recorded or sent anywhere.
strings.xml.scan_permission_denied: Camera access was denied. You can enable it in your device settings, or paste the key by hand instead.
strings.xml.contact_delete_confirm: Delete this contact and the whole conversation? This cannot be undone.
strings.xml.contact_blocked_notice: Blocked. Messages from this contact are rejected.
strings.xml.tutorial_pin_title: Your PIN, and only your PIN
strings.xml.tutorial_pin_body: Everything in Whospair is locked behind a PIN you choose at the next step. Forget it and nothing can be recovered.
strings.xml.tutorial_pin_f2: A duress PIN (set in Settings) erases everything when typed — use it if you are coerced or in danger
strings.xml.tutorial_pin_f3: No fingerprint or face unlock: someone can force your finger onto the sensor, not a code out of you
strings.xml.tutorial_pin_note: When the app goes to the background, it locks itself.
strings.xml.tut_welcome_body: Messages and calls that leave no trace on a server, because there is no server.
strings.xml.tut_welcome_f1: End-to-end encrypted, no account: the keys belong to you
strings.xml.tut_welcome_f2: A message goes out when your contact has the app open, or "Stay reachable" turned on
strings.xml.tut_welcome_f3: The dot next to Tor: green, online; orange, connecting (sometimes a minute)
strings.xml.tut_add_body: No username, no phone number: you exchange keys. Scan their code, or let them scan yours.
strings.xml.tut_add_f1: To confirm: arrived with your link only. Their messages arrive, but they can't call or nudge you
strings.xml.tut_add_f2: Confirmed: you added or accepted them
strings.xml.tut_add_f3: Verified: face to face, you scanned each other's security codes. No one slipped in between you
strings.xml.tut_write_body: Every message has a lifetime chosen when sending; when it ends, it disappears on both sides.
strings.xml.tut_write_f1: Shorter is safer: what is on screen is still on the disk
strings.xml.tut_write_f2: Delete for everyone: removes your messages on your contact's phone
strings.xml.tut_write_f3: Two-way erase: if you both agree, either of you can erase everything, for both, at any time
strings.xml.tutorial_discreet_f4: Camera (optional): the screen hides when you look away, when someone else looks, or whenever it isn't your face. It all happens on the phone, nothing is recorded
strings.xml.tutorial_discreet_f5: "Lock Whospair" tile in quick settings: the app closes in one tap
strings.xml.verify_hint: Face to face, scan each other's code
strings.xml.verify_body: Show this code to your contact and scan theirs. If they match, no one slipped in between you.
strings.xml.verify_fail: This code doesn't match. Don't trust this contact until it's cleared up.
strings.xml.wipe_off: Off. If you propose it, your contact will have to accept.
strings.xml.wipe_asked: Waiting for your contact to agree.
strings.xml.wipe_to_answer: Your contact proposes that either of you can erase everything, for both, at any time.
strings.xml.wipe_on: On: either of you can erase everything, for both, at any time.
strings.xml.wipe_confirm: The whole conversation will be erased on both phones. This can't be undone.
strings.xml.settings_gaze_owner_hint: The screen opens only for you
strings.xml.face_intro_body:
The screen opens only when you are the one looking at it. For anyone else, or if no one is looking, it stays black.

If your face changes (injury, swelling, beard, glasses), it may no longer be recognized and the screen will stay black. At the bottom of the screen, "Turn off hiding with the PIN" always works with your unlock code. You can then record your face again.

This button follows the same rules as the lock screen: your duress PIN, typed here, erases everything, and so do 10 wrong codes.

It protects against prying eyes; it is not a lock: your PIN remains the real protection. Everything happens on the phone: your face is kept as encrypted numbers, never as a photo.
strings.xml.face_enroll_body: Look at the screen for a few seconds, with your face well lit.
strings.xml.face_enroll_fail: Face not recognized. Move into the light, look straight at the screen, then try again.
strings.xml.face_disable_pin: Turn off hiding with the PIN

strings_call.xml.call_delay_hint: Through Tor, your voice arrives about a second late. Leave a short pause before answering.
strings_call.xml.call_unreachable: Not reachable right now. Try again in a moment.
strings_call.xml.call_mic_denied: The microphone is off for Whospair. Allow it in Android settings to call.
strings_call.xml.call_not_confirmed: Confirm this contact first. Only confirmed contacts can call each other.
strings_call.xml.call_log_busy: Call: they were already on a call

strings_design.xml.conversations_empty_body: Add someone by scanning their code, face to face. You can write to them when you both have the app open.
strings_design.xml.discover_code_caption: This code holds your public keys and your Tor address. Nothing else.
strings_design.xml.memory_advice_body: Whospair keeps its keys in memory only while the app is open. But some phones copy part of their memory to storage to seem larger (“virtual memory”, “memory extension”). A key copied that way could stay on the phone after Whospair closes.
strings_design.xml.memory_advice_how: To turn it off: look for “virtual memory” or “memory extension” in the phone settings, turn it off, then restart the phone.
strings_design.xml.mic_denied: The microphone is off for Whospair. Allow it in Android settings to send a voice message.

strings_phase6.xml.ring_peer_offline: %1$s is not in the app right now
strings_phase6.xml.indicator_channel_live:
Tor is running and your address is published. Contacts who also
        have the app open can reach you, and you can reach them.
strings_phase6.xml.indicator_channel_none:
Tor is not ready. Nothing can be sent or received,
        and nothing is being held anywhere for later.
strings_phase6.xml.indicator_tunnel_on:
Your traffic is leaving through a VPN
        interface. Whospair can see that much, and no more — it does not know
        which provider, or whether the tunnel leaks.
strings_phase6.xml.indicator_tunnel_off:
Your traffic is leaving directly. Your
        network provider can see that this device uses Tor, and when — not who
        you talk to, nor what is said.
strings_phase6.xml.vpn_advice_body:
Whospair encrypts what you say, and Tor hides who
        you say it to. Neither hides that you use Tor: whoever carries your
        traffic sees it, at what times, and how often. A VPN moves that view to
        the tunnel operator instead. That is a real change when the party
        watching is the one you are worried about.
strings_phase6.xml.vpn_advice_caveat:
A VPN is not a guarantee. You are choosing
        who gets to watch, not removing the watcher. Pick one you have reason to
        trust, and prefer one you pay for over one that pays for itself with
        your traffic.
strings_phase6.xml.chat_unconfirmed_banner: This person added you with your link. You have not confirmed who they are.
strings_phase6.xml.chat_blocked_banner: Blocked. They can no longer reach you.
strings_phase6.xml.settings_safety_hint: Compare it with your contact in person or by a call. Same number on both phones = no one in between.
strings_phase6.xml.settings_confirm_trust: I have checked — confirm this contact
strings_phase6.xml.settings_block_hint: A blocked contact can no longer connect or send you messages.
strings_phase6.xml.settings_delete_confirm: Delete this contact and all messages? If they still have your link, they may come back as unconfirmed — block them to prevent that.

strings_profile.xml.profile_photo_hint: Cropped to 256 px, metadata removed, sent only over Tor.
strings_profile.xml.profile_photo_error: This image could not be read.
strings_profile.xml.settings_gaze_shield_body: The front camera looks at who is in front of the screen. Everything stays on the phone: no image is kept or sent. Android's camera light stays on while Whospair is open, and the battery drains faster. Turning the phone face down on a table always blacks out the screen.
strings_profile.xml.settings_gaze_onlooker_hint: A second face behind you. Reduces the risk without removing it: a face seen from the side, far away or in the dark can go unnoticed.
strings_profile.xml.gaze_manual_hint: The PIN turns it off, for example in a dark place.
strings_profile.xml.gaze_auto_hint: Off from 8 pm to 6 am, when light is short.
strings_profile.xml.alert_someone: Someone is trying to reach you
strings_profile.xml.nudge_unreachable: Not reachable right now: Whospair is closed on their side.
strings_profile.xml.private_mode_off_hint: You are online and reachable in this conversation.
strings_profile.xml.private_mode_on_hint: You are no longer reachable in this conversation.
strings_profile.xml.private_mode_banner: Private mode is on for this conversation. You can only be reached for one minute after sending a message. To stay reachable, turn off private mode.
strings_profile.xml.file_allow_save_hint: Otherwise it only opens inside Whospair.
strings_profile.xml.file_view_once_hint: Erased on your contact's phone after the first opening.
strings_profile.xml.file_too_big: File too large: 25 MB at most.
strings_profile.xml.file_viewer_pending: This type of file will soon open inside Whospair.
strings_profile.xml.notice_you_forwarded: You forwarded "%1$s"; the sender is told
strings_profile.xml.notice_you_shared: You shared "%1$s"; the sender is told
strings_profile.xml.notice_you_saved: You saved "%1$s"; the sender is told
strings_profile.xml.notice_you_opened: You opened "%1$s" elsewhere; the sender is told
strings_profile.xml.file_open_elsewhere_hint: Whospair cannot display this file. "Open with…", at the top, lends it for a moment to another app, without copying it; the sender is told.
strings_profile.xml.share_sender_told: The sender will be told, without knowing who you send it to.
strings_profile.xml.delete_selected_body: Erased from this phone right away, without waiting for their lifetime. Anything not sent yet will not be sent. Your contact's copy disappears at the end of its own lifetime.

strings_reach.xml.settings_stay_reachable_body:
When the app is closed, your address stays online. Your contacts can write to you and call you.

Messages that arrive are stored as they are, still encrypted, and sealed a second time: they can only be opened with your PIN. Unknown people who have your link have to wait until the app is open.

A notification says only "Whospair is buzzing you": no name, no content. For a call, open Whospair, enter your PIN, then answer — your contact keeps calling for a minute.
strings_reach.xml.settings_stay_reachable_costs: The price: your onion key stays in memory while the app is closed, Android shows a permanent notification, your address is online around the clock, and the battery drains faster. After a restart of the phone, nothing runs until you enter your PIN.
strings_reach.xml.settings_reach_battery_hint: Without this, Android may put Whospair to sleep and you will stop being reachable.
strings_reach.xml.settings_reach_notifications_off: Notifications are off for Whospair: messages will still wait for your PIN, but nothing will tell you they arrived.
strings_reach.xml.settings_reach_hide_hint: Android requires a "Reachable" notification while Whospair stays reachable. You can hide it: the service keeps running, and the state shows in the app, next to Tor.
strings_reach.xml.reach_channel_alert: Someone is trying to reach you
strings_reach.xml.reach_call_text: Open Whospair and enter your PIN to answer.

strings_relief.xml.settings_background_hint: The same for every conversation. The main screens take its colours.
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_live_body: Whospair keeps nothing waiting on a server. A message leaves when your contact has the app open, or has turned on “Stay reachable”.
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_live_f1: The dot next to Tor: green, you are online; orange, connecting
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_live_f2: The first connection can take a few seconds, sometimes a minute
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_live_f3: “reachable” under a name: the contact is there, right now
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_confirm_body: One scan is enough to talk. But someone who only has your link arrives as “To confirm”.
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_confirm_f1: Compare the safety number, in person or on a call
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_confirm_f2: Same number on both phones: no one in between
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_confirm_f3: Only confirmed contacts can call you and nudge you
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_discreet_body: Protections for the moments when someone is next to you.
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_discreet_f1: Phone turned face down on the table: the screen goes black
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_discreet_f2: Reading code: a conversation stays hidden until the code
strings_relief.xml.tutorial_discreet_f3: Private mode: this contact can only reach you when you write to them
strings_relief.xml.chat_peer_outdated: This contact uses a version of Whospair that is too old. Nothing passes until they update — the update itself still reaches them.
strings_relief.xml.share_app_sub: Send the app itself, no store needed
strings_relief.xml.delete_everyone_body: “For everyone” also erases your contact's copy, without any notice. If they can't be reached, it leaves as soon as they are, while Whospair stays open.

strings_security.xml.lock_attempts_left: %1$d attempts left before everything is erased
strings_security.xml.lock_error: Something went wrong while opening. Try again.

strings_security.xml.settings_duress_failed: Not set: the current PIN is wrong, or the duress PIN is too short, identical or of a different length.

strings_settings.xml.read_lock_on_hint: Messages are hidden. Enter the code to read them during this visit.
strings_settings.xml.read_lock_open_hint: Readable until you leave this conversation.
strings_settings.xml.read_lock_banner: Messages hidden. Unlock reading in the settings.
strings_settings.xml.read_code_mismatch: The two codes differ. Start again.
strings_settings.xml.settings_pin_changed_duress_removed: PIN changed. Its length changed, so the duress PIN was removed: set it again with the same length.
strings_settings.xml.settings_pin_rejected: Not changed: this PIN is too short or is your duress PIN.
strings_settings.xml.settings_duress_same_length: Same number of digits as your PIN.
strings_settings.xml.settings_default_ttl_hint: Used in every conversation until you pick another one there.
strings_settings.xml.settings_mask_all_hint: One code for every conversation not hidden yet. Those with a code keep theirs.
strings_settings.xml.settings_mask_all_done: Done. Each conversation now asks for the code.
strings_settings.xml.settings_wipe_confirm: Erase keys, contacts and messages right now? Nothing can be recovered. The app will start over as if newly installed.
strings_settings.xml.settings_new_identity_confirm: New keys and a new address: your current link and QR code stop working. All contacts and messages are erased — your contacts will need to add you again. The app restarts.
strings_settings.xml.settings_restart_tor_confirm: Restarting Tor restarts the app. You will enter your PIN again.
strings_settings.xml.about_body:
A messenger for people who have sensitive things to say to each other. What is said in Whospair exists only on the two phones, for the time chosen, and nowhere else.

No server. No server relays, stores or sees your exchanges. Each phone is its own access point on the Tor network; messages go directly from one to the other.

No account. No number, no e-mail, no real name. Your identity is a key pair created on this phone. You add each other by scanning a QR code, in person or through a link.

End-to-end encrypted. Messages, voice notes, files and calls are encrypted before they leave the phone, then travel over Tor, which hides your IP address.

Ephemeral. Every message has a chosen lifetime, then disappears on both sides. Nothing is backed up anywhere else.

Live. You can only reach someone who has the app open, or who turned on “Stay reachable”.

Protected on the phone. Everything is encrypted under your PIN. Ten wrong PINs, or the duress PIN, erase everything.

Disclaimer. Whospair is a tool. How you use it is your sole responsibility. It is provided as is, without warranty, and its authors cannot be held liable for its use or its consequences.
strings_settings.xml.privacy_body:
Whospair collects nothing. No server receives your data: so there is no one to analyse it or hand it to a third party.

What the app never does: profiling, selling data, advertising, tracking code, crash reports sent anywhere, reading your address book, location. No third-party company receives anything, neither data nor usage signals: the app only talks to the Tor network, to your contacts and to its update distributor.

What stays on this phone, encrypted: your keys, contacts, messages and files — until they expire, you delete them, or after 10 wrong PINs. Photos you send are stripped of their metadata (location, device model).

What others can still see: your network operator can see that this phone uses Tor, but not with whom or what. Your contact sees what you send them, and your profile photo if you allow it.

Updates. While the app is open, it regularly asks, over Tor, whether a newer version exists (at most every 30 minutes). This request contains only its version number: no identity, no contacts, no messages.

Why so often? Because every new version becomes mandatory 5 days after it arrives: an up-to-date version then refuses to communicate with an older one. This is deliberate: an old version may contain a flaw. Without updating, you could no longer reach your friends or colleagues; only the update still gets through to you.

Whospair is constantly evolving, hence frequent updates. A flaw can be discovered and exploited before anyone even notices. Fixing quickly keeps your data out of the wrong hands.

Your rights. Since nothing is collected, there is nothing for us to show, correct or delete. Everything is in your hands: uninstalling the app erases it all.

Responsibility. You alone are responsible for what you send, to whom, and what you do with what you receive. Whospair is provided as is, without warranty.
strings_settings.xml.version_fingerprint_hint: Fingerprint of the certificate that signed this app. Compare it with the one published by the author: if it differs, this is not the genuine app.

strings_update.xml.update_body: Updates come from your contacts, over Tor, with no server. Each version is signed by the developer: Whospair checks the signature before downloading, then the file against it, and Android checks that it is signed with the same key as the app you have. A modified app is always refused.
strings_update.xml.update_available_body: Version %1$s (%2$s) is offered by one of your contacts. It downloads while Whospair is open; if the connection drops, it resumes where it stopped.
strings_update.xml.update_permission_hint: Android must first allow Whospair to install updates. Allow it, come back, then tap again.
strings_update.xml.update_relaying: You pass version %1$s on to your confirmed contacts.
strings_update.xml.update_import_invalid: This package is not signed by the Whospair developer, or it is damaged. Nothing was installed.
strings_update.xml.update_import_installing: Signature verified. Android will ask you to confirm the installation.
strings_update.xml.update_import_relaying: Signature verified. This phone now passes this version on to your confirmed contacts.
strings_update.xml.update_import_mismatch: This is your version, but the app installed here is not the same file. Nothing to pass on.
strings_update.xml.update_import_older: This package is older than your version. Nothing was installed.
strings_update.xml.update_failed_memory: Not enough memory to download it.
strings_update.xml.update_failed_corrupt: The file received does not match the signature. It was discarded.
strings_update.xml.update_failed_signature: This version is not signed with the same key as your app. Refused.
strings_update.xml.update_diffuser_retry: Source unreachable, new attempt in 10 s
strings_update.xml.update_interrupted: Update interrupted, new attempt in 30 min
strings_update.xml.update_mandatory_body: A newer version of Whospair has been available for more than 5 days. Install it to keep using the app: your up-to-date contacts no longer accept older versions.
